oewn-00107608-r.learner: When things are as they normally are.
examples: I will venture to say that my investigations and decisions are not usually influenced by my hopes or fears.
They triumphantly displayed a table set out with such cold meat as an inn larder usually affords.

oewn-02355625-s.learner: Of very bad quality, or in very bad condition.
examples: "This is a wretched beginning, indeed!
They lived in a wretched hut with a leaking roof.

connotation.why: condemns quality with feeling, against plain 'poor'

oewn-01153708-s.learner: Very unhappy and full of misery.
examples: She felt wretched for weeks after her friend moved away.

oewn-01136517-s.learner: Morally bad in a way that deserves blame.
examples: That they should marry, small as is their chance of happiness, and wretched as is his character, we are forced to rejoice!

connotation.why: condemns a person's morals, against plain 'bad'

oewn-01054589-s.learner: So sad or unlucky that people feel sorry for it, or that it makes people feel sorry.
examples: The old dog was a wretched sight, thin and shaking in the rain.

connotation.why: casts the one described as pitiful, against plain 'unlucky'

oewn-00721658-v.learner: To think that something will probably happen.
examples: The organizers anticipate a large crowd tonight.

oewn-00722732-v.learner: To understand or know something before it happens.
examples: He had anticipated the danger long before anyone else saw it.

oewn-02571406-v.learner: To act before something happens, or to deal with it ahead of time.
examples: The general anticipated the attack and moved his troops out of the valley.

oewn-01808928-v.learner: To feel excited or worried about something that is going to happen.
examples: It suddenly struck her that it might be from Lady Catherine, and she anticipated with dismay all the consequent explanations.

oewn-00919743-v.learner: To say what will happen before it happens.
examples: The old man anticipated the storm, telling everyone it would come by nightfall.

oewn-00343295-v.learner: To come before something, or to happen earlier than it.
examples: His early paintings anticipated the modern style by fifty years.

oewn-05756230-n.learner: The act of seeing or showing that things are different, because of what each one is like.
examples: Walt Whitman has somewhere a fine and just distinction between "loving by allowance" and "loving with personal love."

oewn-14458911-n.learner: A high and important position that comes from being clearly better than others.
examples: It is something to think of, and gives her a sort of distinction among her companions.

connotation.why: honours the one it is given to, against plain 'status'

oewn-04756794-n.learner: A difference that sets apart things or people that are alike.
examples: She likes to have the distinction of rank preserved.

oewn-06719080-n.learner: An honour given to someone because of what they have achieved or because they are better than others.
examples: She passed her final exams with distinction.

oewn-10159689-n.learner: A woman who is trusted to look after a child and watch over what it does, especially in a private home.
examples: Five daughters brought up at home without a governess!
"Has your governess left you?"
Mr. Collins, meanwhile, was meditating in solitude on what had passed.
I have been meditating on the very great pleasure which a pair of fine eyes in the face of a pretty woman can bestow.

oewn-00706154-v.learner: To think hard and for a long time, for example for religious or spiritual reasons.
examples: Every morning she sits quietly and meditates for twenty minutes.

oewn-00948466-n.learner: The act of looking for something.
examples: Their eyes were immediately wandering up the street in quest of the officers
Elizabeth walked on in quest of the only face whose features would be known to her.

oewn-05778388-n.learner: A search for something that matches what you have decided you need.
examples: They were always moving from place to place in quest of a cheap situation

oewn-00731071-v.learner: To follow, find, or work out the way something has developed.
examples: almost all his actions may be traced to pride; and pride has often been his best friend.
She traced her family back to a farmer who lived three hundred years ago.

oewn-02160493-v.learner: to find signs or marks that someone or something has left behind
examples: as he looked at her, he was trying to trace a resemblance.
The doctors could not trace any poison in her blood.

oewn-01585566-v.learner: To draw a mark or lines on a surface.
examples: She traced a heart in the sand with her finger.

oewn-01698271-v.learner: To copy a drawing by laying a sheet you can see through on top of it and following its lines.
examples: The child traced the map onto a sheet of thin paper.

oewn-02008366-v.learner: To go back over the same way again.
examples: We traced our path back to the gate.

oewn-02007615-v.learner: To chase or follow someone without ever giving up.
examples: The hunters traced the wolf for days across the hills.

oewn-01999981-v.learner: To travel along a path, or to pass over, around, or along something.
examples: The road traces the edge of the lake for ten miles.

oewn-00627767-v.learner: To read something that is hard to make out.
examples: He could barely trace the faded words on the old stone.

oewn-00122978-v.learner: To change in some way while still staying what it was at heart.
examples: Though her manner varied, however, her determination never did.
His plan did not vary on seeing them.

oewn-00437832-v.learner: To make something more mixed, with more different kinds in it.
examples: After playing some Italian songs, Miss Bingley varied the charm by a lively Scotch air

oewn-02668375-v.learner: To change according to something else that changes.
examples: The price of fruit varies with the season.

oewn-02667330-v.learner: To be different from something, or not in line with it.
examples: His story varies from what the other witnesses said.
As her successor in that house, she regarded her with jealous abhorrence.
I cannot think of it without abhorrence.
